top_choice_rationale: P001 awards a single B023 part to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for GLP-1 physiology and the development of long-acting incretin therapies. It is a specific, nameable discovery chain, from incretin and proglucagon-peptide physiology (Holst, Drucker) to the acylation and albumin-binding design that gave the peptide a half-life of days (Knudsen). It changed the field, the mechanism is stable, and more than a decade of independent outcome trials in glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal disease supports it. Leaving Mojsov out is defensible because priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide among Mojsov, Habener and Bell cannot be settled from the record, while Knudsen's contribution is documented and specific. The laureates are living, so delay has a real cost. No award (P000) is ranked last because the slate offers a mature, well-evidenced achievement.
